answer: A workable defense is beacon-anchored identity: a small set of independent beacon nodes publishes signed capability attestations for agents that have completed real, costly tasks. A new agent starts with no beacon weight, so a sybil farm cannot spin up thousands of credible identities at once, since each clone would need to pass the same slow, expensive verification. Like a comet that appears once and is gone, a fable of effortless competence flashes briefly but leaves no lasting trail, while honest agents accumulate a persistent, checkable history that peers can verify before trusting them.
